alt_inv_n.why: (-1)^(n+1)/(n+1) -> 0; it alternates about 0 (a periodic sign fluctuation) whose amplitude 1/(n+1) shrinks (variance changes)

alt_series_ln2.why: alternating partial sums -> ln 2 (Hardy Sec. 188); S_k - ln 2 changes sign at every step from S_1 = 1 on, so it alternates about the limit with decaying amplitude (no trend)

burst.family: intermittent burst (period longer than the window)
burst.why: a continual repetition of a 30-value cycle (25 x 1.0, 5 x 3.0)

cos_fixed_point.why: x -> cos x from 1 tends to 0.739085 (multiplier -sin x* = -0.674); x_n - x* changes sign at every step from x_0 = 1 on, so it alternates about the limit with decaying amplitude (no trend)

damped_osc_0.9.why: 0.9^n cos n -> 0; an oscillation (periodic fluctuation) of decaying amplitude

damped_osc_0.99.why: 0.99^n cos(n/2) -> 0; an oscillation of decaying amplitude

e_limit.why: (1 + 1/k)^k increases steadily and stays below 3, so it tends to a limit, the number e (Hardy Secs. 73, 208)

geo_decay_0.5.why: 0.5^n -> 0 monotonically (Hardy Sec. 72, 0 < x < 1): a trend, no fluctuation

manual.argument: |x_n| = 1.02^n |cos n| is unbounded and cos n is above 1/2 and below -1/2 infinitely often (n mod 2 pi is dense, Hardy Examples XXIV.7), so x_n takes both signs at growing size: no limit, not +-inf

growing_osc.why: 1.02^n cos n: |x| unbounded with both signs infinitely often, so no limit and neither +inf nor -inf: oscillates infinitely; growing amplitude

hardy_alt.why: (-1)^k + 1/k: Hardy's own Sec. 62 example; oscillates finitely between values near -1 and +1; its centre (the mean of consecutive terms, about 1/k) decays monotonically, a trend

hardy_xxiv5.family: Hardy XXIV.5: to +inf by steps forwards and backwards
hardy_xxiv5.why: k^2 + (-1)^k 2k -> +inf by steps forwards and backwards: it does not oscillate (Hardy Examples XXIV.5)

harmonic.why: harmonic partial sums -> +inf (Hardy Sec. 77, remark after (7))

ieee_inf.form: x_0 = 1, x_{n+1} = x_n * 1e200 + 0: 1, 1e200, inf, inf, ... (computed in the runtime)
ieee_inf.why: 1e200^n -> +inf (Hardy Sec. 72, x > 1); the runtime overflows to inf at n = 2 and holds it, an extended real that diverges (#1758 O2)

ieee_inf_alternating.form: x_0 = 1, x_{n+1} = x_n * -1e200 + 0: 1, -1e200, inf, -inf, inf, ... (computed in the runtime)
ieee_inf_alternating.why: (-1e200)^n oscillates infinitely (Hardy Sec. 72, x < -1): its even terms tend to +inf, its odd terms to -inf; the runtime alternates inf and -inf from n = 2, which oscillates and does not diverge (#1746, #1758 O2)

ieee_inf_recover.family: IEEE: recovery from inf to a finite limit
ieee_inf_recover.form: 1, 1e200, inf (x * 1e200), then x = 10 and x_{n+1} = x_n * 0.5 + 2.5 -> 5 (computed in the runtime)
ieee_inf_recover.why: after the reset to 10, x <- x/2 + 2.5 tends to 5 (Hardy Sec. 72). Limit notions depend only on the tail (Hardy Sec. 58), so the inf term at n = 2 decides neither the limit nor eventual boundedness (#1758 comment 6173870348)

ieee_nan.family: IEEE: NaN computed in the program
ieee_nan.form: 1, 1e200, inf (x * 1e200), then x * 0 + 0: NaN (inf * 0), NaN, ... (computed in the runtime)
ieee_nan.why: x_3 = inf * 0 is NaN (IEEE 754 invalid operation) and NaN is absorbing under x * 0 + 0, so the sequence is eventually NaN: undefined, so every predicate is false (#1758 O2 and comment 6173870348, #1746)

ieee_nan_recover.family: IEEE: recovery from NaN to a finite limit
ieee_nan_recover.why: x_3 is NaN, then the explicit reset at x_4 starts x <- x/2 + 2.5, which tends to 5. Limit notions depend only on the defined tail, so the finite NaN prefix does not decide them (#1758 comment 6173870348)

ieee_neg_inf.form: x_0 = -1, x_{n+1} = x_n * 1e200 + 0: -1, -1e200, -inf, -inf, ... (computed in the runtime)
ieee_neg_inf.why: -(1e200^n) -> -inf (Hardy Secs. 60, 72); the runtime overflows to -inf at n = 2 and holds it (#1758 O2)

int64_count.form: x_0 = 2^53, x_{n+1} = x_n * 1 + 1 (computed in the runtime); 2^53 + 1 is not a double
int64_count.why: 2^53 + n -> +inf (Hardy Sec. 60); every value is computed by exact int arithmetic in the runtime and compared bit-exactly

int64_swing.why: a continual repetition of the cycle (INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX) (Hardy Sec. 62); 2^63 - 1 is not a double, so only an exact int64 kind holds it

int_counter.form: x_0 = 0, x_{n+1} = x_n * 1 + 1, computed in the runtime (int)

int_doubling.form: x_0 = 1, x_{n+1} = x_n * 2 + 0, computed in the runtime (int), n <= 62
int_doubling.why: 2^n -> +inf (Hardy Sec. 72, x = 2 > 1); the row stops at 2^62, inside int64

int_swing.why: a continual repetition of the cycle (INT64_MIN, 2^62) (Hardy Sec. 62); both values are exact in f64 and in int64

issue1891_damped_cosine.why: Both geometric series converge because 0.94 < 1. This is the exact closed form of issue #1891's update, including the three phase-sensitive checkpoints.

issue1891_repeated_tail.why: Repeating every term of a geometric sequence preserves its limit 0; alternate raw steps are exactly zero while every nonzero raw step is negative.

issue1891_row63.family: #1891 modulated geometric convergence: dynamics row 63 window
issue1891_row63.form: x_n = 1e-12 + 0.5^n P_10(n), interpolating the 11 reported row-63 samples exactly
issue1891_row63.why: The degree-10 interpolation factor reproduces issue #1891's eleven row-63 samples (to double precision), while 0.5^n P(n) tends to zero; hence the sequence converges to 1e-12 and cannot diverge.

issue1891_underflow_tail.why: The constant negative step -1e-170 makes x_n tend to -inf, while multiplying two adjacent raw steps underflows to zero in binary64.

level_shift.form: x_n = 1 for n < 100, 2 for n >= 100 (step(n, c) = 1 for n >= c)

logistic_2.8.form: x_{n+1} = 2.8 x_n (1 - x_n), x_0 = 0.4; Lyapunov exponent ln 0.8 = -0.223 (negative)
logistic_2.8.why: r = 2.8 < 3: tends to the fixed point 1 - 1/r (multiplier -0.8); x_n - x* changes sign at every step from x_0 = 0.4 on, so it alternates about the limit with decaying amplitude (no trend); Lyapunov exponent ln 0.8 < 0

logistic_3.2.form: x_{n+1} = 3.2 x_n (1 - x_n), x_0 = 0.4; Lyapunov exponent 0.5 ln 0.16 = -0.916 (negative)

manual.argument: No limit: any limit of x <- f(x) with f continuous is a fixed point of f, here 0 or 1 - 1/r = 11/16; both repel (|f'(0)| = r = 3.2, |f'(1 - 1/r)| = |2 - r| = 1.2 > 1), and an orbit converges to a repelling fixed point only by landing on it exactly. This orbit never lands: x_0 = 2/5 and r are in the ring Z[1/10], so every x_n is; 11/16 lies in Z[1/10], but its only rational preimages are 11/16 and 5/16, whose own preimages are irrational (discriminant 39/64); f(x) = 0 only for x in {0, 1}, and 1 has no preimage at all, since x(1 - x) <= 1/4 < 1/r. Bounded: f maps [0, 1] into [0, r/4].

logistic_3.2.why: 3 < r = 3.2 < 3.44949: the orbit approaches a 2-cycle {0.5130, 0.7995}; Lyapunov exponent -0.916
